concepts.name: RBI as the Sole Currency Authority: Note Issuance and Legal Tender
key_dimensions: Minimum Reserve System (MRS) vs. Proportional Reserve System — when India switched and why
RBI issues all currency EXCEPT ₹1 coin and ₹1 note (issued by Ministry of Finance) — classic UPSC trap
Legal tender status: limited vs. unlimited legal tender distinction for coins vs. notes
Clean Note Policy and currency management obligations under RBI Act, 1934

concepts.name: Banker to the Government: RBI's Role as Government's Fiscal Agent
key_dimensions: RBI manages accounts of Central Government as a matter of obligation, but State Governments by agreement — key distinction
Ways and Means Advances (WMA) to Centre vs. States: limits, interest rates, and conditionalities
RBI's role in government borrowing: Open Market Operations (OMO) vs. primary market subscription
Conflict of interest: RBI as debt manager vs. monetary policy authority — why PDMA was proposed

concepts.name: Banker's Bank and Lender of Last Resort
key_dimensions: CRR and SLR as instruments of statutory pre-emption vs. prudential regulation
Lender of Last Resort (LoLR): emergency liquidity vs. moral hazard concerns
Repo, Reverse Repo, and Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) — hierarchy of liquidity windows and who can access what
Why LoLR function does NOT extend to NBFCs in the same manner as scheduled commercial banks

concepts.name: Monetary Policy Framework and the MPC: Mandate, Composition, and Accountability
key_dimensions: Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework: 4% ± 2% CPI target — legal basis under amended RBI Act Section 45ZA
MPC composition: 3 RBI members (including Governor as Chair with casting vote) + 3 GoI nominees — who holds majority?
Failure clause: what constitutes failure, and the written explanation mechanism to Parliament
MPC vs. RBI Board: MPC decides repo rate; RBI Board does NOT — institutional separation trap

concepts.name: CRR vs. SLR: Instruments, Purposes, and Asymmetries
key_dimensions: CRR: held with RBI in cash, earns NO interest; SLR: held by bank itself in approved securities — key structural difference
Eligible assets for SLR: government securities, cash, gold — NOT corporate bonds (common trap)
CRR applies to Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL); understanding what is excluded from NDTL
Floor and ceiling: RBI Act prescribes no statutory floor/ceiling for CRR post-2006 amendment — RBI has full discretion

concepts.name: Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF): Repo, Reverse Repo, and MSF Architecture
key_dimensions: Policy Repo Rate as the single policy rate since 2011; Reverse Repo = Repo − 25 bps (floor); MSF = Repo + 25 bps (ceiling) — the corridor
Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) introduced in April 2022: absorbs excess liquidity WITHOUT collateral — replaced reverse repo as effective floor
MSF: banks can borrow against SLR securities up to a certain % of NDTL even by dipping below statutory SLR — emergency provision
Difference between LAF (overnight/short-term) and Long-Term Repo Operations (LTRO)/Targeted LTRO (TLTRO)

concepts.name: Open Market Operations (OMO) and Government Securities Market Management
key_dimensions: OMO: RBI buys/sells G-Secs in secondary market to inject/absorb durable liquidity — NOT to finance government deficit directly
Operation Twist: simultaneous purchase of long-term and sale of short-term securities to flatten yield curve — RBI's unconventional tool
Distinction between OMO for monetary management vs. Government borrowing management (primary market)
G-SAP (Government Securities Acquisition Programme): commitment-based OMO introduced during COVID — significance for market confidence

concepts.name: Regulatory and Supervisory Functions: Commercial Banks vs. NBFCs vs. Cooperative Banks
key_dimensions: RBI regulates Commercial Banks under Banking Regulation Act, 1949; Cooperative banks under dual regulation with State Registrars — Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act 2020 expanded RBI powers over urban cooperatives
NBFCs: RBI regulates but does NOT supervise all NBFCs equally — scale-based regulation (SBR) framework post-2021
Payment Banks and Small Finance Banks: who licenses, who supervises — RBI's exclusive domain
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs): supervised by NABARD on behalf of RBI — supervisory delegation trap

concepts.name: Foreign Exchange Management: RBI's Role Under FEMA vs. FERA
key_dimensions: FERA (1973) was criminal in nature; FEMA (1999) is civil — paradigm shift from conservation to management
RBI manages forex reserves; decides current account vs. capital account convertibility limits
Market Stabilization Scheme (MSS): sterilization of forex inflows — RBI issues securities on behalf of GoI to absorb rupee liquidity
RBI intervenes in forex market to prevent excess volatility, NOT to target a specific exchange rate — nuance for UPSC

concepts.name: Priority Sector Lending (PSL): Mandates, Categories, and Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs)
key_dimensions: Domestic commercial banks: 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC); Foreign banks with <20 branches: 40% (phased); those with ≥20 branches: 40% — differentiation by bank type
Sub-targets within PSL: Agriculture (18% of ANBC including 8% to Small/Marginal Farmers), Micro-enterprises, Weaker Sections
Shortfall routing: banks failing PSL targets must deposit in RIDF (NABARD), NHB, MUDRA etc. — not a fine but an opportunity cost mechanism
PSLCs: tradable certificates allowing banks to meet PSL targets by buying surplus from others — market-based compliance mechanism

concepts.name: RBI's Role in Payment and Settlement Systems: PSS Act 2007
key_dimensions: Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007: RBI as the sole regulator and supervisor of payment systems in India
NPCI: set up by RBI and IBA — it is NOT a government body but a 'umbrella organisation' for retail payments — common misconception
RBI's role vs. SEBI's role: RBI oversees government securities settlement (CCIL) while SEBI oversees equity settlement — jurisdictional overlap trap
Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs), card networks, and UPI: all under RBI's PSS Act purview; recent inclusion of Big Tech in payment aggregator regulations

concepts.name: Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework: Triggers, Restrictions, and Exit
key_dimensions: Three risk thresholds based on Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR), Net NPA ratio, and Return on Assets (RoA) / Leverage ratio
PCA restricts: dividend distribution, branch expansion, management compensation, new lending — NOT a moratorium on deposits (distinguish from Section 45 moratorium)
PCA applies to Scheduled Commercial Banks (excluding RRBs and Small Finance Banks historically) and now extended to NBFCs
Exit from PCA: requires sustained improvement across all parameters for at least four quarters — Board's recommendation to RBI

concepts.name: Differential Rate of Interest and Directed Credit: RBI's Developmental Role
key_dimensions: RBI's developmental/promotional function — often ignored but explicitly stated in RBI Act preamble
Setting up of development finance institutions: NABARD (1982), NHB, SIDBI, EXIM Bank — RBI was initial promoter/shareholder of all
RBI divested its stake in NABARD and NHB to Government of India — current ownership structure is a factual trap
Interest rate deregulation: RBI has deregulated lending rates (MCLR/External Benchmark), but certain categories like savings deposits and export credit still have prescribed rates

concepts.name: External Benchmark-Based Lending Rate (EBLR) vs. MCLR: Transmission Mechanism
key_dimensions: MCLR (2016) replaced Base Rate (2010) which replaced BPLR — evolution and why each was introduced
EBLR mandatory for floating-rate retail and MSME loans since October 2019 — links bank lending rates directly to RBI repo rate
Why monetary policy transmission was weak under MCLR: banks' cost of deposits is sticky vs. policy rate — structural problem EBLR addresses
Spread over benchmark: banks can charge risk premium + business strategy premium over EBLR but cannot change spread during loan tenor — consumer protection angle

concepts.name: RBI's Supervisory Tools: On-site Inspection vs. Off-site Surveillance (OSMOS)
key_dimensions: Annual Financial Inspection (AFI) as primary on-site tool; CAMELS rating framework used in assessment
OSMOS (Off-site Monitoring and Surveillance): early warning system using data returns filed by banks
RBI's power to remove bank management, supersede Board, and recommend license cancellation under Section 35A, 36AA of Banking Regulation Act
Difference between RBI-imposed moratorium (Section 45) and DICGC insurance trigger — ₹5 lakh deposit insurance covers per depositor per bank

concepts.name: Capital Adequacy and Basel Norms Implementation in India: RBI's Role
key_dimensions: India follows Basel III; RBI mandates minimum CRAR of 9% (vs. Basel III's 8%) — India is more conservative, a frequent comparison point
Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB): 2.5% of RWA; Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB): activated/deactivated by RBI based on credit cycle
Additional Tier-1 (AT1) bonds controversy: Yes Bank AT1 write-down — RBI's position on hierarchy of bail-in instruments
Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs): SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank — higher capital surcharge, no-failure expectation, 'too big to fail' moral hazard

concepts.name: RBI's Independence vs. Government of India: Section 7 of RBI Act and Institutional Tensions
key_dimensions: Section 7 of RBI Act: Central Government CAN issue directions to RBI Board 'in public interest' after consultation — never formally invoked until 2018 controversy
RBI Board vs. MPC: Board manages overall administration; MPC sets policy rate — different accountability structures
Transfer of surplus to Government: Bimal Jalan Committee (2019) on Economic Capital Framework — what constitutes contingency risk buffer vs. revaluation reserves
Fiscal dominance vs. monetary dominance: when government's borrowing needs conflict with RBI's inflation mandate — structural tension relevant for essay/GS3

concepts.name: Financial Inclusion Initiatives Driven by RBI: BC Model, Jan Dhan, and Digital Finance
key_dimensions: Business Correspondent (BC) model: banks can use agents for last-mile delivery — BC is agent of bank, not independent; liability rests with bank
Differentiated banking licenses: Payment Banks (deposits up to ₹2 lakh, no lending) vs. Small Finance Banks (universal bank-like but focus on small borrowers)
RBI's Account Aggregator (AA) framework: consent-based financial data sharing — RBI regulated entities as Financial Information Providers (FIPs) and Users (FIUs)
Digital Lending Guidelines (2022): loan disbursement only to borrower's bank account, not third-party lending service provider — consumer protection against predatory fintech

concepts.name: RBI and Inflation: Types of Inflation Measures and Which RBI Targets
key_dimensions: RBI targets CPI (Combined) — NOT WPI; WPI is used for GDP deflation and input cost analysis but NOT monetary policy anchor
Core inflation vs. headline inflation: RBI monitors core (ex-food and fuel) as supply-side shocks to food/fuel are outside monetary policy control
CPI basket weights: Food and Beverages ~45.86% — heavy food weight makes CPI volatile and creates dilemma between real economy and inflation targeting
Conflict: supply-side food inflation cannot be controlled by rate hikes (demand compression tool) — limits of monetary policy, calls for supply-side fiscal response

concepts.name: Regulation of Cooperative Banks: Dual Regulation Problem and 2020 Reforms
key_dimensions: Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs): RBI regulates banking functions; State Registrar of Cooperative Societies regulates management/membership — classic dual regulation gap exploited in PMC Bank crisis
Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act 2020: gave RBI power to supersede board of UCBs and recommend amalgamation/reconstruction without State government consent
State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs): regulated by NABARD (not RBI directly) for supervisory purposes — distinction trap
Multi-State Cooperative Societies (banking): fall under Central Registrar and RBI — different from single-state cooperatives
